script_spans: EXT. BANNOCK HARBOR - NIGHT
Mara stands, braces, and fires the flare into the soaked blankets amidships.
Then the diesel catches and the MARGARET ROSE goes up -- a column of fire standing on the black water
Crow touches a road flare to the mortar fuse. The Fourth of July stash goes up -- white and gold chrysanthemums blooming over the burning boat
The anchor line, burned through at the chock, parts. The burning boat swings free and begins to drift
she DIVES -- off the skiff into the black water, surfacing in the firelight, swimming hard for the mooring buoy
Danny throws the skiff into gear, takes up the slack, and eases the burning boat's head around -- slow, straining, the flames roaring overhead
Sam in the bow in a life vest two sizes too big, one hand knotted in Barnacle's collar. The old dog rides like a figurehead

correction.remedy_detail: 1. Pyrotechnics & Fire: If practical pyrotechnic materials or fireworks are used on set, ensure use is under controlled conditions, provide advanced notification to appropriate departments and involved performers, engage a licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator, and obtain required permits from the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) in compliance with CSATF Safety Bulletin #16. Alternatively, execute the burn and fireworks sequences via visual effects or controlled staging. 2. Water Hazards: If practical night water work is staged, make appropriate water safety devices (e.g., life vests, life preservers, safety rings, buoys) available for all personnel working in or around water, implement a personnel accounting plan (such as a buddy or check-in/check-out system) per CSATF Safety Bulletin #17, and take steps to prevent hypothermia per Actsafe Safety Bulletin #17. 3. Staging & Casting: Clarify planned shooting methods, jurisdiction, and casting to determine any additional staging safeguards.
